quote: the cache MUST NOT use that stored response without revalidation unless all the presented request header fields nominated by that Vary field value match
if and only if those in the first request can be transformed to those in the second request by applying any of the following
adding or removing whitespace, where allowed in the header field's syntax
combining multiple header field lines with the same field name (see Section 5.2 of [HTTP])
normalizing both header field values in a way that is known to have identical semantics, according to the header field's specification
reordering field values when order is not significant; case-normalization, where values are defined to be case-insensitive
If (after any normalization that might take place) a header field is absent from a request, it can only match another request
A stored response with a Vary header field value containing a member "*" always fails to match.
The "Vary" header field in a response describes what parts of a request message, aside from the method and target URI, might have influenced
Vary = #( "*" / field-name )
A Vary field value is either the wildcard member "*" or a list of request field names, known as the selecting header fields
A proxy MUST NOT generate "*" in a Vary field value.
Vary expands the cache key required to match a new request to the stored cache entry.
its combined field value consists of the list of corresponding field line values within that section, concatenated in order
A recipient MAY combine multiple field lines within a field section that have the same field name into one field line
The order in which field lines with the same name are received is therefore significant to the interpretation of the field value
field-name = token
Field names are case-insensitive and ought to be registered within the "Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) Field Name Registry"
A field value does not include leading or trailing whitespace.
token = 1*tchar
A recipient MUST parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements
#element => [ element ] *( OWS "," OWS [ element ] )
All content codings are case-insensitive and ought to be registered within the "HTTP Content Coding Registry"
